name: Ayn Rand
role: Russian-born American novelist and philosopher; founder of Objectivism (1905–1982)
summary: Rand advocated reason, rational self-interest and rights-based laissez-faire capitalism, with a government limited to police, courts and defence and funded voluntarily in principle. She opposed the draft, welfare, antitrust and all initiation of force, held abortion to be a woman's right, rejected religion and collectivism including racism, and refused the conservative and libertarian labels.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Called any claimed right to economic security, medical care included, an attempt to enslave producers for the benefit of others, and listed medical care among the false 'rights' of liberals.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Held that wages and prices in a free economy are set by supply and demand and not by anyone's need or decree; statutory wage-setting is a form of intervention she opposed throughout.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Argued that a free market sums up all participants' choices and is the only system compatible with reason; controls only produce dislocations.

public-ownership.rationale: Equated public ownership of the means of production with ownership of the mind and said public property is always captured by a ruling clique.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Argued that higher taxes on the rich come out of investment capital, reducing production and jobs, and that 'soak the rich' appeals are based on ignorance.

property-fundamental.rationale: Called the right to property the only implementation of the right to life and said without it no other right is possible.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Opposed antitrust law and regulation of business as a mess of contradictions that criminalizes business; defended big business as a persecuted minority.

cut-welfare.rationale: Rejected welfare-state transfers as confiscation and told Donahue that aid to the disabled should be only private charity, not tax-funded; her dependency rationale was not the one she gave.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Said communists and Nazis should both be free to speak, since evil ideas are dangerous only by default of better ones; government may not abridge speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Insisted on 'a government of laws and not of men' with officials bound by law in every act, and condemned dictatorship; a leader bypassing the legislature runs against this.

state-harmful.rationale: Denied that the state is unnecessary: argued that even a perfectly moral society needs a government to hold retaliatory force under objective law, and called anarchism irrational.

abortion-legal.rationale: Wrote that abortion is a moral right left to the woman's sole discretion, and that an embryo has no rights.

more-religion-public.rationale: Treated faith as the negation of reason, called the religious-conservative program a substitution of theocracy for capitalism, and wanted state and economics separated as state and church are.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Answering a West Point cadet she said prejudice was dying out under capitalism and denounced racial quotas as institutionalized racism; she rejected group-based redress.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Called the U.N. a corrupt institution that lent respectability to Soviet Russia and delivered victims into aggressors' power.

free-trade.rationale: Said the essence of capitalism's foreign policy is free trade: abolition of trade barriers, protective tariffs and special privileges.

nation-first.rationale: Called for a foreign policy dedicated to the defence of America's rights and national self-interest, repudiating foreign aid and 'international self-immolation'.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Mixed: said a free nation has the right to invade dictatorships but no duty to liberate others at the price of self-sacrifice; opposed Vietnam-type wars and the draft that makes them possible.

limit-growth.rationale: Denounced the ecology movement's opposition to industry and growth as an attack on human survival and rising life expectancy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Presented technology as the ultimate step of knowledge and credited capitalism and freedom, with technology, as the answer to human misery.

revolution-justified.rationale: Held force to overthrow a political system is justified only against tyranny, citing the American Revolution.

central-planning.rationale: Rejected state planning: said the more controlled economies of history start wars and that totalitarian economies end in poverty.

socialized-markets.rationale: Rejected public ownership of production in any form and held that only private ownership makes a free market possible.

basic-income.rationale: Rejected the idea of any entitlement to unearned income from the state; said no one has a claim on others' labor and that aid should be voluntary charity.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Named protective tariffs among the trade barriers capitalism abolishes.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Described government direction of the economy as a mixed economy of pressure groups and favoritism and demanded separation of state and economics.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Defended wage labour and money as the means of voluntary trade, with wages set by mutual consent on the free market.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Her book carried Alan Greenspan's essay arguing for a gold standard and free banking; she herself wrote that government should keep out of money, but she did not discuss central banks as such.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Called welfare-state arrangements that keep private property under government control fascist in principle, and condemned rule by pressure groups.

one-party-rule.rationale: Condemned dictatorship and the communist and Nazi parties alike as variants of collectivism.

democracy-best.rationale: Defined democracy as unlimited majority rule and called it a form of collectivism; she preferred a constitutionally limited republic.

direct-votes.rationale: Said voting is only a device within strictly limited constitutional bounds and favoured representative government; direct majority rule on laws is the unlimited rule she called tyranny.

workers-councils.rationale: Rejected collective bodies as the basis of power; held that only a constitutionally limited government protecting individual rights is proper.

right-to-secede.rationale: Mixed: denied any group or ethnic right to secede, but said a province may secede from a dictatorship or mixed economy to establish a free country.

natural-rulers.rationale: Said no man has the right to rule other men and that political authority comes from the consent of the governed.

political-violence-never.rationale: Held that force is proper in retaliation against those who initiate force and that revolution against tyranny is justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Called wars the second greatest evil that societies can perpetrate, after dictatorship.

separate-church-state.rationale: Called for a separation of state and economics 'in the same way and for the same reasons as the separation of state and church'.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Taught that reason is the sole guide to knowledge and action, rejected faith, and held that law must rest on objective rights, not revelation.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Called competing private governments an absurdity and said that force must be placed in one objectively controlled institution.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Said ethnicity confers no special rights and is not a valid political consideration.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Taught that the interests of rational men do not clash and rejected the idea of enmity between classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said equality means equality before the law and that egalitarians seek to abolish the consequences of virtue and choice.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Told West Point cadets that Native Americans had no right to the land because they lacked property rights and a settled society.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Argued that rational selfishness is a virtue and altruism is immoral.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rejected the claim that rights impose duties to the state or community and held that a man's life belongs to himself.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Attacked ecology's 'harmony with nature' for ignoring man's needs and survival; held that man must alter nature to live.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Credited industry with tripling Europe's population and raising life expectancy, and told readers to thank the nearest smokestack.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Held that restricting technology means restricting the mind and that technology advances human life; she did not address disruption to institutions.

restore-past-order.rationale: Distanced herself from conservatives who defend the existing order without principle and called herself a radical for capitalism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said a country needs a policy based on long-range principles, i.e., an ideology, and attacked 'anti-ideologists' and pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Rejected mass civil disobedience that violates others' rights and said unjust laws must be fought ideologically.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Ridiculed the idea of men returning to 'grunting subanimals digging the soil with their bare hands'.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Praised the free choice to specialize and trade products as the basis of capitalism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Said need is no claim on others, that misfortune is not a mortgage on achievement, and that the principle of redistribution is communist.

production-for-use.rationale: Defended profit and trade by mutual advantage; said rewards should follow the value others voluntarily pay for.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Held that on a free market economic value is set by voluntary consent and that profit comes from production enabled by investment.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Named communism, fascism and absolute monarchy as forms of tyranny and rejected rule by any class.

collective-farming.rationale: Opposed collective and public ownership of productive property in general.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Argued the reverse: capitalism is the only system fundamentally opposed to war, and statism needs it.

taxation-theft.rationale: Contested: held that in a free society payment for government would be voluntary and called redistribution treatment of men as chattel, but did not call all taxation theft and treated a transition as a distant goal.

harm-principle.rationale: Said government may use force only against those who initiate force or fraud and may not penalize ideas.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Said a nation, like any group, has no rights other than those of its individual citizens, and denied that there are group rights.

conscription.rationale: Called the draft the worst violation of individual rights in a mixed economy and 'involuntary servitude'.

positive-liberty.rationale: Rejected the equation of economic power with political power and the idea that a hungry man is unfree; freedom means absence of coercion.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Called racism, the ascription of intellect and character to genetic lineage, a collectivist doctrine of brutes.

organic-representation.rationale: Backed representation of individuals and their principles through chosen agents, not group-based bodies.

total-state.rationale: Condemned the state directing every sphere as fascism and communism, and called for a government limited to protecting rights.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said free countries need no war and that statism needs war to loot; aggression violates rights.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Called for 'a government of laws and not of men' in which officials act only as law permits.

bound-labor.rationale: Said no one may be bound to labor for others and called forced service involuntary servitude and slavery.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Taught that reason and logic give objective knowledge, for which each person is the sole judge but which is not relative to power.

universal-morality.rationale: Held that morality consists of following reason and applies to everyone, even the least intelligent; her ethics rested on man's nature.

single-common-good.rationale: Rejected 'the common good' as capitalism's justification and held that rights belong to individuals.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Sided with Israel against its Arab neighbours as an advanced civilization, while calling it politically a mixed economy leaning to socialism; she did not frame it as a historic right to the land.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Defended the owner's right to run his business and opposed government or worker control of firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Told Donahue she opposed publicly funded education and wanted parents to educate their own children; she opposed state funding.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Published Alan Greenspan's argument that deficit spending is hidden confiscation of wealth, and attacked inflation as a policy of the welfare state.

economic-freedom.rationale: Presented capitalism as the necessary corollary of political freedom and said freedom is the fundamental requirement of the human mind.

national-self-determination.rationale: Mixed: held national self-determination applies only to free societies or those seeking freedom, not to dictatorships that enslave their citizens.

force-without-un.rationale: Called the U.N. a monstrosity and held that a free country may act in its own interest regardless of international bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Said reason is man's only means of knowledge and that faith is the negation of reason.

class-collaboration.rationale: Held that the interests of rational men do not clash, which includes employers and employees dealing by voluntary trade.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Said women may enter any career of their choice and rejected sex-specific legal roles; her view was that government should treat people as individuals.

ban-interest.rationale: Defended interest on loans as payment for risk that lets beginners start producing.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Called racism and legal racial classification a violation of individual rights, and criticised even majority 'racism by law'.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Described a proper government as an agent of citizens' self-defense and rejected the notion of a ruler-versus-ruled class order.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Defended oil companies' right to produce free of controls and ridiculed ecologists' attacks on industry; she did not speak of expanding output as such.

national-mission.rationale: Said a free nation has no duty to liberate others at its own cost, though it may; her foreign policy was national self-interest.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Told Donahue's audience that in America anyone can get anything regardless of sex by showing ability and that feminists wanted government handouts.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Held government may use force only against those who initiate force and treated procreation as a matter of individual choice.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Said the only proper functions of a government are the police, the army and the law courts.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Denounced racism as collectivism and judged people by character, not lineage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Defined equality as equality before the law and of inalienable rights held by every human being.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Said white settlers represented the progress of the mind and had the right to the continent; she defended Israel on the same ground.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Held that all citizens are equal before the law, but she did not discuss religious personal law.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Said the Constitution rightly forbids governmental establishment of religion; she also opposed state-run education altogether.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Said that a state should be limited to protecting rights and condemned statism and dictatorships.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said the source of governmental authority is 'the consent of the governed' and that government is the citizens' servant.

population-transfer.rationale: Held government may use force only against those who initiate it, and criticised collective treatment of people by group.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Stated that no man, group, society or government has the right to initiate physical force against others.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Said competition is a by-product of productive work, not its goal, and that interests of rational men do not clash.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Said that there can be no political crimes under American law and that the government may not take cognizance of a person's ideology.

separated-powers.rationale: Praised the American system of checks and balances as an incomparable achievement limiting government power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Opposed communism and any party claiming to rule by ideology through force.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Said poverty is not a mortgage on others' labor and that life is not 'one huge hospital'.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Located the cause of poverty in lack of capitalism and individual freedom, not in population.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred: she held that rights are not subject to override and the government's only role is protecting them; she did not address emergency powers directly.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Said prices are set by supply and demand and that each control creates dislocations requiring more controls.

party-controls-media.rationale: Held that freedom of speech means freedom from government interference and suppression.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Defended a free nation's sovereignty and attacked international bodies; she did not discuss the EU specifically.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rejected rule by faith and theocracy, and held that government is limited to protecting rights.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Held a free country has the right of self-defense and defended its war effort against dictatorships; she opposed unjust wars and the draft, not defence as such.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Held that government may not suppress ideas or publications and said even pornography is protected speech.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Held property rights to include the right to use and dispose of material values, so forcing owners not to rent violates them.

people-in-arms.rationale: Endorsed a volunteer army as the proper, practical way to defend a free country.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Held that cultures differ in value, calling some societies primitive and others civilized.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Held reason must govern knowledge, rejected faith, and opposed government establishing religion.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Called hard-core pornography disgusting but opposed legal suppression as a threat to freedom of speech.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Said that freedom is a precondition of productivity and that controls cause dislocation.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Called for repudiating foreign aid and said a country has no duty to sacrifice for others.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Rejected the 'common good' as justification and held that property rights come from right to life.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Described Soviet Russia as a statist dictatorship of the collectivist kind, not as capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Attacked ecologists' appeals to avoid risk as aimed at technology and progress.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Said the Constitution is a limit on government and should forbid establishing religion; government should not control religion either.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Rejected mystic authority and held rulers as servants of the citizens.

character-from-environment.rationale: Insisted on free will, with character the result of choices, and rejected both genetic and environmental determinism.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Said government officials may do only what law permits, subordinating might to right.

leader-cult.rationale: Condemned dictatorship and mystic authority and held that government is servant, not ruler.

land-redistribution.rationale: Called the redistribution of wealth the basic principle of communism and a claim to treat human beings as chattel.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Said ethnicity does not endow anyone with special rights, and rights belong only to individuals.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Said ideas are not crimes in a free society and only the initiation of force may be penalized.

women-must-cover.rationale: Held that only force against others may be legally restrained, not private conduct.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Rejected ethnic or ancestry-based political claims as collectivist.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Said there are no group rights, only individual ones.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Held that philosophy and ideas determine the character of social systems.

ban-cartels.rationale: Called the antitrust laws unenforceable and said coercive monopolies arise only from government privilege, so breaking up business is not the remedy.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Said a majority has no right to vote away minorities' rights and that the Constitution limits government.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Opposed quotas and government preferences by sex or race and said the way to opportunity is ability.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Called for free trade across borders and no tariffs.

moral-incentives.rationale: Held that morality means rational self-interest and rewards follow productive achievement.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Called a minority's seizure of power a putsch, not a revolution; force in violation of rights is gang warfare.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Said the rise of capitalism swept away aristocracy and titles of nobility and that rights must not be infringed by such institutions.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Contested: held that more civilized settlers had the right to take land from nomadic tribes, but that a free nation has no duty to rule or liberate others.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Denounced quotas in employment and education as racism by law and hoped the Supreme Court would rule against them.

public-money-creation.rationale: Endorsed the gold standard and free banking as protection against government money creation.

delink-world-market.rationale: Held that economic progress follows from freedom and trade and faulted statism for poverty.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Held that workers in a free economy gain, not lose, from capitalism, and that wealth comes from production.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Said private individuals may choose not to associate or support others, and was opposed to anti-discrimination laws in the private sector; she called racism evil in itself.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Said a constitution that places individual rights beyond reach of public authorities delimits political power.

elective-rulers.rationale: Said government rests on consent of the governed and opposed hereditary titles.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Held that tyranny may be overthrown by force, as in the American Revolution, and officials bound by law.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Denied that there is any moral duty to help others and called charity a marginal matter.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Attributed poverty to lack of capitalism and individual freedom, not exploitation.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Held that those who built free institutions on the continent had the right to it and denied special claims of birth.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Called communists and Nazis variants of the same evil notion, collectivism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Told cadets that the contradiction of slavery had to be eliminated and that the Civil War did so.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Held that individual rights and a limited government apply universally and called dictatorships outlaws.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Held that the military's sole role is defending against foreign invaders and that it must be subordinate to law.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Opposed government restrictions on private trade and ownership.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred: she opposed government-run social programs and favoured voluntary arrangements, though in 1976 she reportedly took Social Security benefits; she did not discuss pension design.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Said any resource made useful by effort should be private property of those who apply the effort.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Rejected racial quotas and judging outcomes by group; held that individuals have rights, not groups.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Called 'consumerism' an anti-concept and denied special rights for consumers.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Held that sovereignty of a free nation is derived from its citizens' rights and must be respected.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said lobbying is the result of a mixed economy of pressure groups, and that money is not political power in a free market.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Held procreation is optional, not a duty, and no one may be treated as a means.

job-guarantee.rationale: Rejected claims to a right to livelihood, saying it means enslaving producers.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Contested: said unjust laws should be obeyed under protest while fighting for repeal and that obedience is not a sanction. She treated respect for legality as important, which cuts against the statement.

non-intervention.rationale: Said free nations have the right to invade dictatorships such as Nazi Germany or the Soviet Union.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: When an audience member alleged an Illuminati of bankers, she said she had never heard of such conspiracies.

religious-nation.rationale: Rejected national definition by religion; held individuals rights are not group-based.

defeat-communism.rationale: Opposed any collaboration or compromise with Soviet Russia and said communist countries aim at world conquest.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Rejected government-funded provision of services in a mixed economy.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Credited capitalism with unprecedented prosperity and freedom in the nineteenth century.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Said women can succeed in the existing system without government help.

socialized-care.rationale: Said no one has a claim on others' services and that private choices should not be collectivised.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Held capitalism to be the only moral system and denounced the 'middle' as a pendulum with no principle.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Said no tribe has a claim merely from birth or past habitation if it did not use or protect rights in the land.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Said she did not approve of homosexual relationships but that it is improper for the law to interfere with consenting adults (per her 1968 Ford Hall Forum answer as reported).

suppress-opposition.rationale: Said the government may not take cognizance of ideology and that free speech protects dissent.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Said ideas are never a crime in a free society.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Held that nations have no right to subject others and condemned statist looting.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Rejected unlimited majority rule and collective decision-making by pressure.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Rejected group-based analyses of oppression, holding that only individuals have rights.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Used 'rightist' and 'leftist' as meaningful terms, defining the former as freedom and capitalism, and the centre as a pendulum.

alienated-labor.rationale: Said capitalism rewards the best of every man and leaves him free to choose and specialize in the work he likes.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Held that the source of authority is the consent of the governed.

social-market-economy.rationale: Rejected welfare-state combinations of market and control as mixed economy leading to dictatorship.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Said a society that renounced retaliatory force would be at the mercy of the first thug.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Said a free nation should defend freedom against communist expansion and called neutrality in principle indefensible.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Held that rulers derive authority from the consent of the governed and condemned hereditary titles.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Defended interest as payment for risk which makes production possible.

property-franchise.rationale: Held that voting derives from the right to life and from rational judgment, excluding only children and the incapable, not those without property.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Rejected both the ecology movement and feminism, held that man must adapt nature to his needs.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Said free speech does not require private owners to finance opposing views, and censorship is a government act.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Said law must be objective and officials bound by it, with no touch of whim in government action.

racial-franchise.rationale: Called racism collectivism and held that rights belong to all individuals equally.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Said that marriage and relationships should be left to individuals' own judgment.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Denied that economic power resembles political power since it can be won only by voluntary trade.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Held that government may not take any stand on ideas and should not compel belief or promote an establishment of thought.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Said government's basic task is to place retaliatory force under objective control, via police, courts and the army.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Said that those unable to work should rely on voluntary charity, though she called charity a marginal virtue.

rent-control.rationale: Opposed price controls as interventions that cause dislocation.

abolish-ip.rationale: Called patents and copyrights the legal implementation of a man's right to the product of his mind.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Rejected state-compelled youth service, which she regarded as statism.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Defended returns on investment and interest as legitimate payment for risk.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Said the right to life implies the right to self-defense, and force is morally imperative in retaliation.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Rejected self-sacrifice as a moral ideal, including sacrifice for the state.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Rejected mysticism and framed politics in terms of reason, rights and force.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Rejected group-based economic claims and held that rights belong to individuals.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Held that public property is a collectivist fiction taken over by a clique.

municipal-property.rationale: Rejected public property and community ownership of means of production.

family-wage.rationale: Said the value of a man's work is set by voluntary agreement on the free market, not need.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Opposed government funding of science and research as an intrusion forcing taxpayers to support ideas.

person-over-state.rationale: Said the individual is the smallest minority and that no man may be treated as a means to others' ends.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Called racism and ethnic collectives primitive collectivism and denied group rights.

racial-pride.rationale: Said racial or ancestral pride is a pseudo-self-esteem unearned by the individual.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Contested: held force is justified only in retaliation and the draft only for unjust wars, yet said any free country may invade a dictatorship.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Rejected ethnic or cultural grounds for political claims.

communal-electorates.rationale: Rejected group-based politics and held that rights belong to the individual.

free-public-college.rationale: Opposed government funding of education and said it breeds dictatorship.

capital-controls.rationale: Called for free international exchange, abolishing trade barriers.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Opposed redistribution via taxation to supplement incomes.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Said poor countries' problem is lack of freedom and capitalism; opposed foreign aid.

sacred-nation.rationale: Said a nation is just a number of individuals and has no rights beyond theirs.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Opposed using taxpayers' money for others' benefit.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Held that economic power comes only by voluntary means and rejected exploitation theories.

public-service-media.rationale: Held that government funding of ideas forces men to pay for opposed views.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Said religion rests on faith, which she held negates reason, with some moral points on a dangerous base.

farm-price-support.rationale: Opposed price controls and government subsidies as privileges.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Held that rights belong to every individual and equal rights under law, and women may enter any career.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Treated ecology as an attack on man's right to survive and opposed regulation on that ground.

premarital-sex.rationale: Told Playboy that an affair or marriage is moral if both take it seriously and it rests on values, and that it is for the two to decide.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Rejected any government cash support; welfare only by private charity.

women-suffrage.rationale: Said voting derives from rational faculty and only the incapable are excluded; she said she would work for female officeholders other than a president.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Said feminists asked for government power and handouts, which she opposed.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Said any resource that requires human knowledge and effort should be private property of those who apply them, and denied tribes land they did not use.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Rejected faith and revelation as negations of reason.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Condemned planned statist economies and communist regimes as slave societies.

national-church-status.rationale: Held government must not establish religion.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Held that no ethnic group has rights beyond individuals, and denied ethnicity any special political standing.

simple-living.rationale: Rejected the glorification of primitive simplicity and praised consumer prosperity.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Said settlers had the right to build on land that natives had not developed.

equal-conscription.rationale: Held that military conscription should not exist for anyone, calling it involuntary servitude.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Rejected tribal and blood-and-soil ties; held that individuals, not nations, have rights.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Held that force may be used only in retaliation by government acting under objective law, with rights of the accused.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Rejected ethnic ties as a basis of political rights.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Held resources become valuable only through human effort and belong to those who apply it.

self-ownership.rationale: Held that the right to life means a man's life and its product belong to him.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Said monopolies arise only from government privileges such as franchises and subsidies.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Held that economic rewards are set by free exchange and earned, not by equality.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Opposed taxes and controls on free exchange.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Said prejudice was dying under capitalism and that today's institutionalized racism comes from quotas.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Contested: said one must comply with unjust laws while campaigning for repeal, and compulsion is no moral sanction.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Held that value stems from mind and voluntary exchange, not labor alone; production is an intellectual process.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Rejected communist party rule and held that a free market requires freedom.

notes: Positions are taken from her own nonfiction, mainly as collected in the Ayn Rand Lexicon, plus the 1964 Playboy interview (quoted there) and 1970s Q&A appearances. Contested points: she personally said she would not work for a woman president but supported women in other offices and equal rights; she called Israel's Arab opponents 'savages', which her audiences contested; in 1976 she reportedly claimed Social Security despite opposing it. Fictional speeches (Galt) were used only where the Lexicon quotes them as her own formulations of positions held in nonfiction.
